record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Random Matrix Theory and the Theory of Integrable Systems. II
record.original_question: Can one explain conceptually how Tracy and Widom’s solution of ASEP works and extend that method to more general initial data for ASEP and related interacting-particle models?

evidence.quote: In another direction, it remains an open, and somewhat mysterious, problem to understand how Tracy and Widom’s solution of ASEP actually ‘works’, and to extend their method of solution to more general initial data.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
The Asymmetric Simple Exclusion Process (ASEP) on the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}$ is the continuous-time Markov process in which each site is occupied by at most one particle, and each particle independently attempts to jump one step to the right at rate $p$ and one step to the left at rate $q$ (with $p+q=1$, $p\ne q$); a jump is suppressed if the target site is already occupied. Given an initial particle configuration $Y\subset\mathbb{Z}$, Tracy and Widom derived exact Bethe-ansatz-type integral and Fredholm determinant formulas for the transition probabilities and for the distribution of the position $x_m(t)$ of the $m$-th leftmost particle at time $t$, in particular establishing convergence of $x_m(t)$, suitably rescaled, to the Tracy–Widom GUE distribution in the case of step initial data $Y=\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$.

Provide a conceptual explanation of why Tracy and Widom's exact-formula method for ASEP works, and extend this method to obtain analogous tractable formulas (and their asymptotic analysis) for ASEP and related interacting particle systems (e.g. $q$-TASEP, stochastic six-vertex, etc.) starting from more general classes of initial data beyond step (and step-Bernoulli) initial conditions — for instance, flat, stationary, half-flat, two-sided Bernoulli, or general deterministic initial configurations.
artifact.status_search_result: Tracy–Widom's exact formulas were originally proved for step and step-Bernoulli initial data. Substantial progress has since been made via duality and Macdonald-process methods (Borodin–Corwin–Sasamoto "From duality to determinants for q-TASEP and ASEP") and via stochastic vertex model approaches, yielding formulas for broader classes of initial data and related models (q-TASEP, stochastic six-vertex). However, a fully conceptual explanation of why the Tracy–Widom Bethe-ansatz method produces Fredholm determinants, and complete extension to general (e.g. flat or arbitrary deterministic) initial data, remains incomplete; the problem is best classified as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Integral Formulas for the Asymmetric Simple Exclusion Process
status_evidence.snippet: Tracy–Widom derive integral formulas for ASEP transition probabilities for general initial configurations bounded on one side.
status_evidence.claim: Tracy–Widom's original method gives formulas for one-sided bounded initial data.

status_evidence.title: From duality to determinants for q-TASEP and ASEP
status_evidence.snippet: Borodin–Corwin–Sasamoto derive Fredholm determinant formulas for q-TASEP and ASEP via Markov duality, providing a more conceptual framework.
status_evidence.claim: Progress on conceptual understanding and extension to related models via duality.

status_evidence.title: Asymptotics in ASEP with Step Initial Condition
status_evidence.snippet: Tracy and Widom prove Tracy–Widom GUE limit for ASEP with step initial condition.
status_evidence.claim: Asymptotic result established only for step initial data initially.
